output:
Dear all,

Just coming up for air after nights and catching up with this properly.

First, I am so happy that Amma and Appa want to come. Having you here for ordinary days, not just a packed fortnight when we try to do everything at once, is something I’m really looking forward to. Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable, including “Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays”. Apparently Amma’s diary is being organised before she has even packed.

Kiran, you’re right that I should have spoken to you earlier. I started the visa paperwork because the agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, and I treated that as an admin job when it was also the moment to bring everyone into the conversation. I’m sorry. You should not have found out that things were already moving through the family announcement.

For a bit of background, the idea first came up on the phone in August, when Rohan showed Appa the vegetable patch and Appa said, “I could grow drumsticks there.” We’ve talked about it since, and I’ve been getting increasingly excited. None of that excuses not telling you sooner.

On Appa’s heart, I don’t want to answer a serious worry with “it’ll be fine”. Dr. Prakash has agreed to review Appa in March before the flight and do a video consultation in July. He’s also happy to share his notes with me, with Appa’s agreement, so we can have the relevant information here. We’ll need to take his advice at the March review about whether the travel plans are sensible.

I’ve also got a travel insurance quote with pre-existing cardiac cover, at about £640 each for the six months. The agent says it covers the stent, but I want that confirmed in the policy wording, including what cardiac treatment and emergency care are covered and any exclusions, before we buy it. We shouldn’t be relying on free NHS treatment. Leicester Royal is fifteen minutes from us, and I know half the cardiology team, which is reassuring practically, but it isn’t a substitute for proper insurance or Dr. Prakash’s review.

The annexe is finished now: ground floor, no steps, and its own shower with a grab rail. You’ll have your own space, Amma and Appa, rather than spending six months living out of suitcases in the children’s territory.

And Kiran, your point about six weeks is fair. Amma, being excited to have you here doesn’t mean expecting you to stay if you’re missing home. The return ticket will be flexible, and you can go home whenever you want. The proposed dates are the first week of April to the end of September 2027. It’s a long-term UK visitor visa, but each visit is limited to six months, so we’ll check the exact dates carefully.

Pune for Ganesh Chaturthi needn’t be lost either. One possibility is for Amma and Appa to fly from here to Pune in September and finish the trip there. Or could the Pune lot come here in August? I’d be very happy to cover your flights. That’s an invitation, not an answer on your behalf about which plan you’d prefer.

Could we all have a video call this Sunday at 4pm UK / 9.30pm India? I’d like us to talk this through properly, including what Amma and Appa want and anything we haven’t thought of yet.

Love,
Meera
